newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAINS NEED RAIN AFTER HOT,DRY MAY-MET OFF.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAINS NEED RAIN AFTER HOT,DRY MAY-MET OFF.

text.p: Hungary's grains have benefited from a hot May but rains forecast for this week would be welcome as the upper soil is quickly losing moisture, the Meteorological Office (OMSZ) said on Tuesday.
"The average temperature for this month was 18.3 degrees Celsius, 3.3 degrees above the 30-year average," Attila Bussay of the OMSZ told Reuters.

He added that despite average upper soil moisture levels between 30 and 40 percent, most crops have made up some of the delay caused by an unseasonally cold April and deeper roots could prove an advantage later in the summer.
"Most plants have grown deeper roots to reach for water, and that would make them more resistant to a summer drought," Bussay said.
He added that the rains forecast for the second half of the week would relieve fears of an imminent drought.
"We expect at least five millimeters of rainfalls next weekend over 70 percent of the country," Bussay said.
